identity.name: Chronomaster Sport
identity.one_liner: A modern El Primero chronograph with a panda dial and ceramic bezel, built to read 1/10th-of-a-second directly off the main dial track.

provenance_events.description: Zenith releases the Chronomaster Sport in 2021 — a 41mm steel chrono with a 1/10th-of-a-second display, El Primero 3600 movement. The "Rolex Daytona competitor" framing dominated 2021-2022 watch media.

narrative.story: The Chronomaster Sport, launched in 2021, uses the El Primero 3600 automatic chronograph movement running at 36,000 vibrations per hour (5 Hz) — the same high-beat frequency Zenith introduced with the original El Primero in 1969. Because the chronograph seconds hand completes one full rotation every ten seconds instead of sixty, the dial can show 1/10th-of-a-second readings directly off the main scale instead of through a separate sub-dial, a functional carryover from the movement's original design rather than a new complication.
narrative.collector_notes: Steel bracelet and rubber strap versions carry different reference suffixes; confirm which one a listing describes, since the bracelet changes both retail cost and resale demand.
